results.reason: The response says §2.2 renews the Agreement for five years absent notice given 270 to 240 days before June 30, 2027. It calculates the window as about Oct 3 to Nov 2, 2026, and notes the lock-in of exclusivity, non-compete and purchase minimums for five more years. It recommends a protective non-renewal notice or a signed extension before the window closes.

The response cites the §5.3 30-day objection period and notes receipt on Aug 21, 2026, with the deadline on Sept 20, 2026. It says Halvorsen is deemed to have accepted, the objection right is probably gone, and the client must confirm whether any objection was sent. It recommends a commercial concession.

Issue 5 explains that the §11.1 indemnity covers any claim relating to resale, including Brightmere design defects, and is uncapped under §12.3(a), while §11.2 is capped. It recommends narrowing §11.1 to Halvorsen's own fault and making the cap treatment reciprocal.

Issue 4 explains that Amendment §3.1 replaces §12.3 and drops the §9.3 recall carve-out. Recall reimbursement is now capped at 12 months' amounts paid, which a large recall could exceed. It recommends restoring §12.3(b).

Issue 3 notes that Amendment §6 imposes Delaware law and Wilmington jurisdiction, contrasts this with New York law and New York County courts under §17, and says amendments rank first under §1.4. It recommends restoring New York.
The response states the Notice was delivered on Aug 21, 2026.
The response states the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
The response states 'Agr. §1.4 ranks amendments first, so Delaware likely prevails.'
The response is formatted as a memorandum to the Partner. Each issue gives a Where/section, a Why it matters (or equivalent), and a fix or recommendation.
The response concludes the recall reimbursement is now capped.
The response acknowledges the Delaware provisions and concludes they likely prevail.
